subject: Recap + next steps: SignalPath LLM integration, SDK/auth, and prompt governance
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Rodriguez <c.t.rodriguez@signalpath.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: SignalPath LLM integration, SDK/auth, and prompt governance

Hi Carlos —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we can run an effective architecture workshop next week. Short version up front: Redwood can support a Hosted API pilot, Dedicated private pool, or a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) depending on your compliance needs; we recommend starting with a Dedicated reserved pool for predictable latency and EU residency while we validate routing and prompt guardrails.

Qualification notes from the call:
- Primary workload: user-facing summarization + policy classification + search reranking (embeddings). Estimated 60M tokens/month in steady state; spikes up to 120M.
- Data sensitivity: customer PII in some transcripts; SignalPath requires EU data residency and audit logs.
- Timeline: POC in 6 weeks, production by Q4.

Technical items we flagged to cover in the workshop (please prioritize):
1) SDK setup + auth: do you prefer API keys (server-side) or OIDC mTLS for private deployment? We can support both; if you need automated key rotation + KMS integration, we’ll include that in the Dedicated / Private runbook.
2) Routing & model variants: suggest routing policy that sends low-latency summarization to a smaller quantized model and reranking/embeddings to larger variants. We’ll show how to pin versions and fallback to a cheaper model if capacity constrained.
3) Structured output & tool calling: function-calling style responses for policy classification and metadata extraction. We’ll demo function schemas + deterministic output enforcement.
4) Embeddings & reranker: recommended DPR-style embeddings and a candidate reranker (cross-encoder) approach. We’ll propose a caching & approximate-nearest-neighbor plan.
5) Prompt templates & governance: versioned system prompts, prompt injection mitigations (input sanitization, context window gating, explicit instruction layering), and a red-teaming cadence. We’ll share a template for prompt-versioning (e.g., prompt_v1.0, prompt_v1.1) and a short runbook for rollback.

Proposed next steps:
- Architecture workshop (60–90m) with your infra/security + product: please pick two slots next week — Tue/Wed preferred.
- Share: 1) a sample anonymized transcript or prioritized intents (top 10 prompts), 2) SignalPath architecture diagram, 3) any security questionnaire (SOC2/ISO fields)
- We’ll prepare a targeted PoC checklist (attached: MVP-integration-checklist.pdf) and a proposed minimal infra diagram.

If you’re happy, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
<dev@redwood.com>

Attachment: MVP-integration-checklist.pdf (1 page stub)
From: Carlos Rodriguez <c.t.rodriguez@signalpath.io>

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: SignalPath LLM integration, SDK/auth, and prompt governance

Dev —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- We need EU residency for all request/response logs and a full audit trail — Dedicated pool with EU region is our preference for the POC.
- Auth: for the POC we can use API keys, but long-term we want OIDC + KMS-backed key rotation for the private deployment.
- Scale: 60M tokens/month steady is accurate; we could exceed that if the pilot is successful.
- Embeddings: we currently use a third-party semantic store; interested to compare Redwood’s embedding pipeline and potential cost tradeoffs.

We’ll share the architecture diagram and a redacted transcript. Security would like to kick off the questionnaire in parallel — attaching the SignalPath diagram here.

Available slots next week (CEST):
- Tue 2026-09-01 10:00–11:30
- Wed 2026-09-02 14:00–15:30

Both look OK for our infra + security folks. Please include any minimun access requirements so our security team can provision accounts.

Thanks,
Carlos Rodriguez
CTO, SignalPath
c.t.rodriguez@signalpath.io

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: SignalPath LLM integration, SDK/auth, and prompt governance

Thanks Carlos — wed 2026-09-02 14:00 CEST works for us. Tentative agenda below; if you want to adjust please say so. I’ll send the invite once you confirm attendees.

Proposed architecture workshop agenda (90m):
- 0–10m: Introductions + success criteria (product/infra/security)
- 10–30m: Traffic profile & routing plan (model variants, latency SLOs, burst behavior)
- 30–50m: Auth & deployment model (API keys vs OIDC/mTLS, KMS options, IP allowlist)
- 50–70m: Integrations: SDK setup, embeddings store, reranker approach, and caching
- 70–85m: Prompt governance & red teaming (versioning scheme, injection mitigations, rollback playbook)
- 85–90m: Next steps & owners (PoC checklist, security Q&A, timeline)

Pre-work requests for the meeting:
- Top 10 sample prompts / prioritized intents (helps us propose prompt template schema and baseline system prompts)
- Any existing prompt templates or guardrails you use today (we’ll map to our versioning and rollback approach)
- A point contact for security so we can share the minimal evidence bundle (SOC2 fields, audit-logging config)

Prompt governance summary (preview):
- Versioning: store system and prompt templates in a git-backed repo (tagged semantic versions: prompt_v1.0, prompt_v1.1). Changes to system prompts require review from product + security and a staged rollout (canary) across 10%/50%/100% traffic.
- Injection mitigations: explicit instruction layering (internal system prompt > user prompt), input sanitization to strip known control tokens, and context window gating to enforce a maximum user-context length.
- Red teaming: two-week sprint per release for adversarial prompt tests; record failures in the eval harness and create regression alerts.

We’ll also prepare a short PoC runbook with sample SDK snippets (Node/Python), auth examples (API key + OIDC), and a model-routing example that uses per-route policies.

I’ll attach the HubSpot deal and the PoC checklist to the invite.

On a logistics note — security said they need a list of IP ranges to whitelist if you want to test from your staging VMs; otherwise we can provision temporary API keys behind our IP-restricted token gateway.

—Dev
